question: True statement regarding insulin:

options.opa: Produced by alpha cells of pancreas
options.opb: Two polypeptide chains are bound by disulfide linkages

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Insulin is a hormone" -> "produced by beta cells of the pancreas" -> "not produced by alpha cells" -> "therefore, option a is false" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Insulin consists of two polypeptide chains" -> "these chains are linked by disulfide bonds" -> "therefore, option b is true" -> 90%
CHAIN: "Insulin facilitates glucose uptake" -> "also affects potassium levels" -> "shifts potassium into the cell" -> "therefore, option c is false" -> 90%
CHAIN: "Subcutaneous insulin has a half-life" -> "approximately 60 minutes" -> "therefore, option d is true" -> 85%
analysis: Insulin is a hormone produced by the beta cells of the pancreas, making option a incorrect. The structure of insulin consists of two polypeptide chains (A and B chains) that are linked by disulfide bonds, confirming option b as correct. Insulin facilitates the uptake of glucose into cells and promotes the movement of potassium into the cells, which means option c is incorrect. The half-life of subcutaneous insulin is approximately 60 minutes, supporting option d as correct. Therefore, the true statements regarding insulin are options b and d, with option b being the most directly related to the structure of insulin itself.
